## The Source Base

### The Pool

**3 sweeps retrieved 36,928 records of which 31,233 were distinct.** The shared rejection store removed 2,971. The subject gate admitted 7,039 and refused 21,223. Deduplication by title and year removed a further 247, leaving **6,792 records, every one of which is cited** across 16 clusters. A further 111 definitions are hand-written, being the primary documents, the books and the back-references to earlier articles in this series.

By source the admitted set is 6,334 from the Crossref registry, 395 from the NASA technical reports server and 310 through the Defense Technical Information Center's registry prefix.

### The Homonyms This Article Measured, and What They Cost

**Three of this subject's words are severe collisions and all three were measured before the first sweep rather than guessed at.** A probe against the registry returned, for a bare `gremlin`, a bone morphogenetic protein antagonist, a children's therapy series, an Oxford English Dictionary headword, a 1943 note in `Notes and Queries` and a horror film. For a bare `gremlins` it returned a reconfigurable-robotics architecture and a statistical package for multipartite networks. **And `retrieval`, which was expected to be mild, turned out to be the worst of them**, because in atmospheric and Earth remote sensing retrieval is the word for inverting a measurement. A probe for `airborne retrieval` returned limb sounders, leaf area index, aerosol polarimetry, methane and trace gas mixing ratios and airborne light detection and ranging, with nothing aeronautical in the first twelve results at all.

**Not one of the three produced a contaminant in the pool, and that is a measurement of query design rather than of filtering.** Because none of the three words was ever asked bare, the records they would have brought were never retrieved, so there was nothing for a filter to remove. **Three candidate store patterns were written and tested against the admitted pool and all three matched zero records**, so none was added. The shared store's discipline is that an entry records the incident that produced it, and a pattern with no incident behind it is a guess with a regular expression around it.

**What did get through is the ordinary kind.** A bare `unmanned aerial vehicle` anchor, written for the first version of the gate, admitted 1,539 records, and a publisher-prefix scan showed what they were, being object detectors, drone photography, aerial geopolitics of policing, inhalation exposure from agricultural spraying, airborne communication relays, magnetometer surveys and a two-dimensional drone swarm for transferring laboratory samples. **The modern unmanned-aircraft literature is one of the largest in engineering and almost none of it is about this article.** The cut was made by subject rather than by platform, and the same defect one level down had a bare `aerodynamic` anchor admitting a paper on road vehicle drag reduction.

### What the Store Cost This Subject, and What Was Opened

The shared rejection store carries 140 curated patterns across 30 tagged families and 728 recorded judgements. **This article added four of those patterns and one of the families**, being the remote-sensing sense of retrieval, the grey partridge and the desert locust behind two programme names, the African locust bean, and molecular docking, which is the new family. **Two families were switched off for this article and the reasons are different.**

`missiles` was opened because the airframe is a cruise missile with wings and the engine is the one in the Tomahawk, so the launch transients, carriage, separation and folding-wing deployment that the pattern deletes are this article's subject.

**`marine` was opened before the first sweep rather than after it**, which is unusual and deliberate. A towed cable in water is the same differential equation in a denser fluid, the underwater literature is much the older and better documented half of it, and the aerodynamic towed-body literature alone would leave this article's keystone nearly empty. That is the precedent set when naval hydrodynamics was admitted to a scaling argument for the same reason. **The price is visible in the towed-body cluster**, which carries a great deal of work on underwater vehicles and ship towing, and the article says so rather than presenting the cluster as aeronautical.

### What the Equation Review Cost the Gate, and What It Found

**The equation-density review promoted five subjects and the reference base had to follow, which is now the eleventh article running.** The first two sweeps asked for airborne recovery, towed bodies, wakes and relative navigation. **They never asked for the drag polar, for feedback design limitations, for the phase a transport delay costs, for aerodynamic damping of a cable, or for attrition modelling**, and the probe measured all five between twenty-six and forty-six records in a pool of nearly six thousand. A third sweep written in those five vocabularies took them to between ninety and five hundred and thirty-nine. **The audit was run before that sweep and not after it**, which is the half of the rule that keeps being lost.

**And reading the third sweep's kept sample found what two earlier readings had missed.** A single off-subject title in a sample of thirty, a measuring method for the drag coefficient of a revetment block, led to a scan that turned up **66 records on molecular docking** sitting in the relative-navigation cluster, being pancreatic adenocarcinoma inhibition, dopamine receptor binding geometries, androgenetic alopecia, kidney stones and the taste mechanism of umami peptides. **The homonym table has named molecular docking since A334 and no pattern had ever been written**, because no article in this series had needed the word until one whose entire subject is docking.

**A qualifier list cannot separate them and that is the lesson.** The phrase `docking and molecular dynamics` is one of the commonest collocations in computational chemistry, and it satisfies any qualifier an aerospace gate would reach for, being dynamics, control or mechanism. The store pattern therefore **requires a drug-discovery companion rather than excluding an aerospace one**, and it is tagged so that an article whose subject is drug discovery can open it. A first version wrote those companions as whole words and `inhibitor` then refused `inhibitors`, **which is the plural-boundary defect this store has now recorded five times**.

### What the Gate Deliberately Does Not Hold

**The payload, the operational concept and the autonomy architecture.** A gate wide enough to hold electronic warfare payloads, distributed effects and machine learning would bring three enormous literatures into a survey about catching an aeroplane, and none of them bears on whether the catch can be made. **A gate that excludes a subject has not measured it**, and this article draws no conclusion about any of the three.

### The Thin Cluster, and Which Kind of Thin It Is

**The keystone cluster is the smallest substantive one in the survey at 120 records.** The first sweep returned 78 and a second sweep written in the field's own vocabulary, asking for aerial recovery and for the mothership, cable and drogue arrangement by name, took it to its present size. **That is the thin-keystone rule firing again and the cure was the usual one.**

**But it stayed small after the cure, and the reason is the third kind of thinness rather than the first two.** A cluster can be thin because the heading is wrong, because the work is filed under another subject, or because the work was never done. **Here it is the third.** Airborne recovery of a flying uncrewed aircraft had essentially not been achieved before this programme, so there was very little to publish about it, and what the cluster does hold is an instructive shape. It is mid-air retrieval of things descending under parachutes from the nineteen sixties onward, a decade of simulation work on the three-body recovery problem from 2009, and then the programme's own paper.

## Epistemic State

### What the Record Establishes

**The register's description of the X-61A is not official Department of Defense wording**, and the compiler says so in a note above the table. The date, the designation, the contractor, the engine and the sponsor are official. The mission statement is not. **This is the first research designation for which that is true**, measured across all 31 X rows.

**The programme ran from 2015 to 2021, from four teams to two to one**, with Phase 1 awarded 31 March 2016, Phase 2 on 15 March 2017 and Phase 3 to Dynetics in April 2018. Five air vehicles were built. **The agency's programme page now states that the programme is complete.**

**Nine sorties were flown in four series for eighteen hours, two vehicles were lost, three remain.** The sorties in the four series sum to the stated total exactly and the airframes built less those lost equals those remaining exactly.

**One airborne recovery was achieved, on 29 October 2021, after at least nine previous attempts each of which came within inches.**

### What Is Computed Rather Than Reported

**The depth of maximum wake gradient behind a transport aeroplane is a fixed fraction of its wing span**, being the span times pi over eight root three, which for the C-130 is 30.1 feet. This is an identity and contains no assumption about weight, speed, density or altitude. **The formation station at 125 feet sits 4.16 times deeper than that, where the gradient is 6.19 times flatter.**

**A passively towed cable settles to an inclination fixed by its own weight and its own drag, and to nothing else.** At 200 knots at 10,000 feet a ten millimetre steel wire rope settles at 14.9 degrees. **A cable that would hang at forty-five degrees would have to weigh 10.4 times what that rope weighs.** The passive geometry therefore does not produce the arrangement the programme used, which is why the docking device is attitude-controlled.

**The X-61A carries 1,922 newtons per metre of span against 3,909 for the cruise missile that shares its engine**, so its induced drag at a given dynamic pressure is smaller by a factor of 4.14. This uses published weights and published spans and no estimate.

**An uncontrolled vehicle leaves a six inch capture window in 0.99 seconds in a one metre per second gust**, and the position loop that holds it needs a bandwidth of about 0.228 hertz, which is 1.3 times the fundamental transverse mode of the cable the docking device hangs from.

**The relative kinetic energy at a 1960 Corona canopy snatch was about 165.1 kilojoules against a few hundred joules for a vehicle that has matched speed**, a factor of 486.

**A flyaway cap of 700,000 dollars and a 20 use life are one requirement**, and its value is 35,000 dollars of airframe per sortie.

### What Is Assumed

**The recovery airspeed, altitude and aircraft weight are not published** and are taken as 200 knots, 10,000 feet and the mean of the C-130A's empty and maximum weights. The wake results scale with all three and the identity for the worst depth does not.

**The cable's diameter and linear density are not published** and three combinations are carried rather than one.

**The wing area, the lift to drag ratio, the zero-lift drag coefficient and the specific fuel consumption are not published.** The wing area is bounded rather than estimated, and the other three are varied across a band.

**The capture window is inferred from the phrase within inches** and is carried at six and at twelve inches.

**The turbulence is represented by a sharp-edged gust**, which is the crudest available model and gives an acceleration rather than a spectrum.

### What the Record Does Not Settle

**The engine.** The official record names an F107-WR-105 and the only published rating for that dash number is twice what every public description of the vehicle states. **This article does not resolve it** and reports both.

**The designation date.** The register says 6 June 2019 and the prime contractor's subcontractor says August 2019.

**The turnaround.** The agency writes twenty-four working hours and the contractor writes approximately twenty-four hours, about the same event.

**The number of docking attempts in the fourth series**, which is why the success rate above is a bound rather than a figure.

**Why the programme stopped.** The agency's page says the programme is complete and its 2021 release says the team would determine next steps. **No cancellation, transition or follow-on decision has been found and none is claimed.**

## Out of Scope

**The payloads and the operational concept.** What the vehicles would have carried and how a volley would have been employed are the reason the programme existed and bear on none of the arithmetic here.

**The autonomy stack.** The vehicle is described as semi-autonomous with one operator controlling up to four or up to eight depending on the source, and the architecture of that autonomy is not examined.

**The wider attritable-aircraft programmes.** The [XQ-58][related_post_a355_x58_slot_taken_by_xq58] and its relatives \[[Kratos XQ-58 Valkyrie][ref_xq58]\] share a procurement philosophy with this vehicle and not its problem.

**Underwater towed bodies**, whose literature this article deliberately admits because the equations are the same, are not treated as a subject in their own right.

**Any assessment of whether the capability should have been pursued**, which is a question about policy and not about whether the catch can be made.

## Conclusion

**The register stops being a primary source at this designation and the article had to change method because of it.** For the [X-60A][related_post_a357_generation_orbit_x60] the government's own sentence about the vehicle could be read closely enough to carry a whole argument. For the X-61A there is no such sentence. The official record is a date, a designation, a contractor, an engine and a sponsor, and everything else in the register's row is a compiler's reconstruction, marked as one. **That is the first time in sixty-two articles that the register has declined to say what an X-plane was for.**

**What it did say, in the one cell that is official, is an engine that disagrees with every public account by a factor of two.** The F107-WR-105 is documented at 1,400 pounds of thrust and the vehicle is universally described with 700. Neither figure changes the conclusions here, because at Mach 0.6 both are several times the drag, and **the published maximum speed is therefore a choice rather than a ceiling on either reading**.

**The vehicle is not a cruise missile and its own published dimensions prove it without a single estimate.** It carries 1,922 newtons per metre of span where the cruise missile sharing its engine carries 3,909, so its induced drag at a given dynamic pressure is 4.14 times smaller. **A vehicle that has to come home and fly formation with a transport has to be efficient at the transport's speed, and span is the only thing that buys that.**

**The hard part is the last few metres and the arithmetic says why.** The worst place to hold station behind a transport is a fixed fraction of its span, 30.1 feet for a C-130, and the programme's formation station sits 4.16 times deeper where the gradient is 6.19 times flatter. A passively towed cable hangs at an angle set by its own weight and drag and cannot be told where to go, which is why the docking device flies. **And the position loop that must hold a vehicle inside a six inch window needs about 0.228 hertz, while the cable that device hangs from responds at 0.176. The loop's crossover sits between the first and second modes of its own target.** That cable is too heavily damped to ring, at a damping ratio of 0.324 on its fundamental, **and the damping removes the ringing without moving the tracking problem**, because a loop cannot reject motion at a frequency it crosses over on whatever produces the motion.

**The C-130 had been catching things in mid-air since 1961 and the difference is that this one was flying.** A Corona canopy snatch engaged at about 165.1 kilojoules of relative energy and needed a winch that could absorb it. A vehicle that has matched speed engages at a few hundred joules and needs nothing of the structure. **The difficulty did not go away. It moved from the hardware into the guidance**, and nine attempts within inches is what that move cost.

**The programme answered the feasibility question and could not begin on the reliability one.** Four vehicles recovered in under thirty minutes was the objective and one vehicle recovered was the result, in a mission that was not attempting the rate. A twenty-use life was the requirement and the whole fleet flew 45 percent of the sorties that one life test needs. **The economics survive that easily, because even five uses brings the airframe cost per sortie to 140,000 dollars, which means twenty was never the break-even.** **And what twenty buys turns out to saturate.** An airframe that can be lost on any sortie delivers the sum of a geometric series rather than its design life, and that sum cannot pass the reciprocal of the loss rate however long the life is. At five percent per sortie the ceiling is exactly twenty, so the requirement is only specifiable if the loss rate is well below it. **The reliability question and the economics question are the same relation asked twice**, which neither half of this article could see alone.

**And the record's last word is a contradiction the series has met before.** The agency's page says the programme is complete. Its own release says the team would analyse the data and determine next steps. **No decision is recorded either way**, which is the [X-60A's][related_post_a357_generation_orbit_x60] ending arriving at a vehicle that flew.
